openings.claim: B (the valued outcome) does not imply M (complete superseded-row references); M alone does not establish B. Remove the global completeness dependency with a per-batch ledger retaining every original, duplicate, unmatched and amendment row. Apply explicit links; preserve recorded alternatives when missing selection relationships prevent choice. For the awkward amendment, record possible double counting; equal quantities do not prove identical events. Use only supplied conversions and dictionary; infer no missing quantities, including from neighboring batches.
openings.discriminator: Hypothetical counterexample: the disturbed copy yields twelve cited reconciled quantities or bounded disagreements while its missing reference stays absent. The nearest rival gates specific-record amendment reconciliation on repairing that reference. The ledger should avoid that dependency without increasing unsupported definite claims; resolved-batch gains remain uncertain.
openings.probe: Compare ledger and ordinary specific-record amendment linking with a completeness gate on both supplied copies. Freeze outputs before opening the sealed per-batch key. Within the extra twenty minutes compare resolved-batch counts, unsupported definite claims and follow-up counts, including whether missing-reference effects stay local. Each workflow retains its sixty-minute review limit. Assume no follow-up answer.
openings.uncertainty: Recorded alternatives and the missing selection relationship must express bounded disagreement without invented quantities. Reserve field-specific requests for the removed superseded-row reference and undefined status dictionary entry, allowing at most one further missing-field or record request. Defeat: any lost row, unsupported resolution, inability to deliver twelve cited outcomes within sixty minutes, or more than three requests. Actual record structure and reviewer capacity remain untested; feasibility and benefit are hypotheses, not observations.
